text:
No. My previous message was wrong. The Great Wall isn't visible to the naked eye from the Moon, and it isn't the only human-made structure visible from there, because none are. From about 384,000 km, even continents-scale features are hard to resolve, and the wall is at most ~10 m wide and similar in color to the terrain around it.

It's also largely not visible from low Earth orbit (~400 km) without aid. Astronauts, including Yang Liwei on China's first crewed flight, have reported not seeing it unaided. Under favorable light and with zoom lenses, it has been photographed from the ISS.
